production_declarations.name: dyadicObservation
production_declarations.finding: At successor n+1 the recursive index n/2 is strictly smaller, including n=0; natural division and omega termination obligation are mathematically valid. The total recurrence gives d0=0 and pairs d(2k+1)=d(2k+2)=1-dk. No horizon or predictor parameter is hidden in the observation sequence.

production_declarations.name: meanPredict_limitNoRegret_iff_mean_converges
production_declarations.finding: Forward uses endpoint limits a0,a1 to get M_T^2 -> -a0 and (1-M_T)^2 -> -a1. Their difference plus1 divided by2 equals M_T identically, so m=(-a0+a1+1)/2. Eventual [0,1] mean membership gives m in [0,1]. Reverse obtains all real-comparator limits -(u-m)^2 from the existing producer and then LimitNoRegret. It does not assume empirical mean convergence in the forward direction. Endpoint sign facts and hmUnit are logically redundant in these body branches, not hidden assumptions or proof defects.

production_declarations.name: dyadicObservation_binary
production_declarations.finding: Strong induction uses n/2<n+1. Complement maps0 to1 and1 to0; base0 is exact. Supplies interval proof without assuming range.

production_declarations.name: dyadicObservation_unit
production_declarations.finding: Both binary values lie in the closed interval. No probability or asymptotic qualification is introduced.

production_declarations.name: dyadic_pair
production_declarations.finding: The parent indices (2k)/2 and (2k+1)/2 both equal k in natural arithmetic; second successor is normalized before unfolding.

production_declarations.name: dyadic_prefix_pair
production_declarations.finding: Writing S(n)=sum_{t<n}d_t, induction appends exactly positions2n+1 and2n+2 and yields S(2n+1)=2n-2S(n). Base n=0 reads S(1)=d0=0.

production_declarations.name: dyadic_high_count
production_declarations.finding: Base exponent0 uses empty horizon4^0-1=0. Successor identity4^(n+1)-1=2(2(4^n-1)+1)+1 is valid because4^n>=1. Applying the prefix recurrence twice gives S(4^n-1)=(2/3)(4^n-1). Nat.cast_sub is guarded by hp.

production_declarations.name: dyadic_low_count
production_declarations.finding: For4^n>=1, 2*4^n-1=2(4^n-1)+1. Prefix recurrence yields S(2*4^n-1)=(2/3)(4^n-1), including n=0 and horizon1.

production_declarations.name: dyadic_high_mean
production_declarations.finding: Uses exponent n+1 so the horizon is at least3. Proves real denominator nonzero before cancellation, obtaining exactly2/3 for every n.

production_declarations.name: dyadic_low_mean
production_declarations.finding: Horizon2*4^n-1>=1, natural-subtraction casts are justified, and the real denominator is nonzero. Division gives1/3-(1/3)/(2*4^n-1), yielding0 at n=0 rather than an erroneous constant1/3.

production_declarations.name: dyadic_horizons_tendsto
production_declarations.finding: Uses4^n -> infinity in naturals; threshold b+1 guarantees both truncated-subtraction horizons eventually exceed b. Both cofinality proofs include the subtraction offset.

production_declarations.name: dyadic_empiricalMean_subsequences
production_declarations.finding: High mean is the exact constant2/3. Low horizon diverges as a real number, so its reciprocal tends to0; substituting the exact low-mean formula gives1/3. This proves both conjuncts, not one selected route.

production_declarations.name: dyadic_meanPredict_obstruction
production_declarations.finding: Assuming a finite comparator0 regret limit a, shared equivalence forces M_T^2 -> -a. Composition with the two cofinal horizons gives -a=4/9 and -a=1/9, contradiction. This correctly uses the squared limits rather than blindly inferring square nonconvergence from mean nonconvergence. The first two conjuncts reuse actual same-predictor producers. The last conjunct extracts the comparator0 limit from LimitNoRegret and contradicts hn; it does not depend on the new all-comparator equivalence. All four conjuncts use exactly meanPredict dyadicObservation.
